To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified 70 differentially expressed genes in HNSCC and that there was a significant clustering of genes in the genome at two chromosomal regions.
we have identified a series of genes that are differentially expressed in hypopharyngea HNSCC and that are potential markers and targets.
differential display analysis of hypopharynx squamous cell carcinoma identified 70 genes with strikingly different expression between tumour and normal tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new diagnostic and therapeutic strategies in HNSCC.
the identification of new markers and therapeutic target genes of HNSCC.
the identification of genes that are differentially expressed in HNSCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results provide the most complete gene expression profile to date of HNSCC.
differential display analysis is a very powerful tool for the identification of new markers in HNSCC.
the differential display technique has provided a new and unique perspective on the molecular biology of HNSCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified 70 novel HNSCC markers, 13 novel genes, 2 novel genomic hotspots of HNSCC disruption and 1 novel gene function (the HNSCC marker gene, HNSCC1, is a novel gene that is involved in the differentiation of keratinocytes).
the expression of a large number of genes is significantly altered in HNSCC and that the majority of these genes are not known to play a role in HNSCC.
the genes we have identified are potentially new markers and therapeutic candidates for HNSCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HNSCC is a highly heterogeneous tumour, with many distinct molecular pathways that are activated during tumourigenesis.
differential display is a powerful technique for gene expression studies and can be applied in a variety of settings.
differential display analysis is a powerful tool for the identification of novel differentially expressed genes.
